cls: Nootropic / cognition enhancer - semisynthetic vitamin B6 (pyridoxine) derivative
quick: Commonly 200 mg orally three times daily (600 mg/day), per European product information
Take with or after food to reduce gastrointestinal upset
Avoid unless clearly necessary; safety not established
Avoid; safety in breastfeeding not established
Caution; limited data - use with care in renal impairment
Caution - hepatotoxicity and cholestasis have been reported
Liver function, full blood count, and skin; watch for hypersensitivity
summary: Pyritinol (pyrithioxine) is a semisynthetic derivative of pyridoxine (vitamin B6) marketed in some European and other countries as a nootropic for cognitive disorders. It is not FDA-approved. Its clinical evidence is limited and it has been associated with serious adverse effects including hepatotoxicity, cholestasis, pancreatitis, blood dyscrasias, and pemphigus-like skin reactions, which has led to restricted or withdrawn use in several markets.
indications: Symptomatic treatment of chronic cognitive disorders / dementia syndromes (per European product information)
Adjunct in some forms of rheumatoid arthritis (historical, limited use)

dosage.n: Per European SmPC; review need periodically

admin: Take with or after meals to reduce stomach upset
Swallow with water; do not take at the same time as antacids/chelating agents unless advised
Re-evaluate benefit periodically as evidence of efficacy is limited
Stop and seek care if jaundice, severe rash, or unusual bruising/bleeding occur
moa: Pyritinol is two pyridoxine (vitamin B6) molecules linked by a disulfide bridge. It is proposed to improve cerebral glucose uptake and metabolism, enhance cholinergic and dopaminergic neurotransmission, and improve red-cell deformability and cerebral blood flow. The precise mechanism underlying any cognitive benefit is not well established.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to pyritinol or pyridoxine derivatives
History of pemphigus or pyritinol-induced skin reaction

preg: Safety in pregnancy has not been established; avoid unless the potential benefit clearly outweighs the risk.
lact: It is not known whether pyritinol is excreted in human milk; breastfeeding should be avoided during treatment.
renal: Data are limited; use with caution in renal impairment.
hepatic: Hepatotoxicity, cholestatic hepatitis, and pancreatitis have been reported. Use with caution and monitor liver function; avoid in significant hepatic disease and discontinue if liver injury develops.

major: Penicillamine and gold (additive risk of pemphigus/blood dyscrasia - structural/immunologic similarity)
moderate: Levodopa (B6-related drugs can affect levodopa - clinical relevance uncertain)
interactions.food: Take with food to reduce GI upset
interactions.diagnostics: May elevate liver enzymes, amylase/lipase, and alter blood counts

counsel: Take with food; report loss of appetite, nausea, or yellowing of skin/eyes
Stop the drug and seek care urgently if you develop blistering skin sores, severe rash, or severe abdominal pain
Tell your doctor about any history of liver disease, autoimmune disease, or reactions to penicillamine/gold
The evidence for benefit in memory disorders is limited - discuss with your doctor whether to continue
pk: Gradual; any cognitive effect develops over weeks of regular use
Plasma peak within a few hours of an oral dose
Short (a few hours); given in divided daily doses
Store at room temperature, protected from light and moisture
pearls: A vitamin B6 (pyridoxine) disulfide-linked dimer marketed as a nootropic (e.g., Encephabol) - NOT FDA-approved; dosing follows European SmPC/product information
Clinical efficacy evidence is weak and it carries notable safety risks (hepatotoxicity, pancreatitis, pemphigus, blood dyscrasias)
Use has been restricted or withdrawn in several countries because of the risk-benefit balance
Structurally and immunologically related to penicillamine - similar autoimmune adverse-effect profile
missed: If a dose is missed, take it as soon as remembered unless it is nearly time for the next dose, then skip it. Do not double up.
overdose: Specific overdose data are limited. Excessive doses may cause gastrointestinal upset, agitation/insomnia, and could worsen hepatic, pancreatic, or hematologic toxicity. There is no specific antidote; manage supportively and monitor liver, pancreatic, and blood parameters.
